title: How an Airbag Works in 60 Seconds 🚗💥 #shorts
description:
An airbag goes from folded to full in about 30 milliseconds. A crash sensor feels the sudden stop, an igniter sets off a small chemical charge, and the burst of nitrogen gas blows the bag out at up to 200 mph. Tiny holes then let the gas escape so the bag cushions you instead of bouncing you back. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#airbag #carsafety #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: An airbag fully inflates in about *30 milliseconds*, faster than you can blink.

steps.label: Sensor
steps.text: A *crash sensor* feels the sudden stop, like hitting a wall at *10 to 15 mph* or more.

steps.label: Igniter
steps.text: It sends an electric signal to an *igniter*, which sets off a small *chemical charge*.

steps.label: Gas
steps.text: The reaction instantly makes a big burst of *nitrogen gas*, the same gas in the air we breathe.

steps.label: Inflate
steps.text: The folded nylon bag *bursts out* at up to *200 mph*.

steps.label: Vents
steps.text: Then *tiny holes* let the gas escape, so the bag *softens* and catches you gently.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Sense, ignite, *inflate*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
